parentQA.a: Yes, when it is done in the open. NIL representation is governed by state law, NCAA rules and the school's own policy. We register where registration is required, every agreement goes in writing, and we file what the school asks for. If something would cost him eligibility, we do not do it. [Ryan: confirm state and school requirements before this goes out.]
Nothing up front. Our fee is a percentage of NIL and marketing income we bring in, stated in the agreement before anything is signed. We walk through the exact terms with you in person.
Ryan Hays, a licensed attorney and NFL contract advisor since 2012. Collective agreements, brand deals, exclusivity, what happens if a coach leaves. He reads all of it before your son signs.

parentQA.q: What if it isn't working at his school?
parentQA.a: Then we have a protocol for that. It is a last resort. The plan is to make it work where he is. If a move is ever the right call, it is made with a short list, a real need on the other end, and everything in writing.
Jack first, then Ryan. Both have his number, and there is no account manager in between.

35 years. Combined 50 years representing NFL players. Six clients who were the highest paid at their position. Jack played and coached. Ryan is a licensed attorney. Call any parent of a current client; we will give you the numbers.
